pages.title: Two shunts change the routes
pages.text:
Two shunts change the routes
Retain pulmonary ﬂow Qp and grouped systemic ﬂow Qs.
The foramen ovale joins the
atria; the ductus arteriosus joins pulmonary artery and aorta.
The placenta is an exchange interface, not free mixing of maternal and fetal blood.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 3 / 18

Declare the positive directions
Qd > 0 : pulmonary artery − →aorta.
Qf > 0 : right atrium − →left atrium .
A sign convention is not yet a one-way ﬂow law.

pages.title: At the pulmonary artery
pages.text:
At the pulmonary artery
Right-pump ﬂow separates into two routes:
QR = Qp + Qd .
If Qp = 100 and Qd = 50, then QR = 150 mL/min.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 5 / 18

pages.title: At the left atrium and aorta
pages.text:
At the left atrium and aorta
Pulmonary return and foramen ﬂow enter the left side:
QL = Qp + Qf .
At the aortic junction,
Qs = QL + Qd.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 6 / 18

pages.title: The fourth balance is not independent
pages.text:
The fourth balance is not independent
Qs = QL + Qd = (Qp + Qf ) + Qd.
Rearrange the sum:
Qs = (Qp + Qd) + Qf = QR + Qf .
The right-atrial balance follows from the other three.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 7 / 18

pages.title: The fourth balance is not independent
pages.text:
The fourth balance is not independent
Qs = QL + Qd = (Qp + Qf ) + Qd.
Rearrange the sum:
Qs = (Qp + Qd) + Qf = QR + Qf .
The right-atrial balance follows from the other three.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 7 / 18

pages.title: Pump output need not equal pulmonary flow
pages.text:
Pump output need not equal pulmonary ﬂow
For (Qp, Qd, Qf ) = (100 , 50, 40),
QR = 150, Q L = 140, Q s = 190 mL/min.
Check both systemic balances:
140 + 50 = 190 = 150 + 40 .
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 8 / 18

pages.title: Zero flow does not establish closure
pages.text:
Zero ﬂow does not establish closure
For a ductus,
Qd = Gd(Ppa − Pao).
Qd = 0 may mean Gd = 0, or may mean equal boundary pressures.
Closure is zero conductance, not zero resistance.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 12 / 18

pages.title: Reversed flow enters the pulmonary junction
pages.text:
Reversed ﬂow enters the pulmonary junction
Take Qp = 300, Qd = −100, Qf = 0.
QR = 300 − 100 = 200 .
The missing 100 mL/min arrives from the aorta through the ductus.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 13 / 18

pages.title: Reversed flow enters the pulmonary junction
pages.text:
Reversed ﬂow enters the pulmonary junction
Take Qp = 300, Qd = −100, Qf = 0.
QR = 300 − 100 = 200 .
The missing 100 mL/min arrives from the aorta through the ductus.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 13 / 18

pages.title: The aortic balance agrees
pages.text:
The aortic balance agrees
QL = 300 + 0 = 300 , Q s = 300 − 100 = 200 .
Of the left-pump output, 100 returns to the pulmonary route and 200 enters the systemic
route.
No blood is created by the negative sign.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 14 / 18

pages.title: Pressure rules do not solve the whole circulation
pages.text:
Pressure rules do not solve the whole circulation
The companion prescribes local pressures and illustrative pulmonary ﬂows.
A full model
must also determine those pressures from chambers, vascular properties, boundary
conditions and blood volume.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 16 / 18

pages.title: The transition changes both pressures and routes
pages.text:
The transition changes both pressures and routes
Pulmonary conditions change; the placental route is removed.
Ductus ﬂow can reverse
while conductance remains positive. Foramen ﬂow can stop under an unfavorable pressure
diﬀerence.
Neither event alone speciﬁes anatomical closure time.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 17 / 18

pages.title: Recover the series circulation as a limit
pages.text:
Recover the series circulation as a limit
If Qd = Qf = 0,
QR = Qp, Q L = Qp, Q s = QL.
QR = Qp = QL = Qs .
Deleting a shunt requires rebalancing the ﬂows.
Mathematical Cardiology Notes 18 / 18
